hook: Foreign investors pulled *₹48,056 crore* out of Indian stocks in October
tldr: Foreign portfolio investors have sold ₹48,056 crore of Indian equities so far in October, citing high crude prices, West Asia tension, inflation and weak earnings. Selling eased last week, with two days of net buying.

beats.what: FPIs are on track for another heavy month of outflows, after big withdrawals last month too.
beats.why: Oil and war risk make emerging markets look riskier; weak company earnings don't help.
beats.care: FPI selling drags the Nifty and weakens the rupee. If you run SIPs, falling markets buy you more units; don't panic-stop them.

cards.body: FPIs are foreign funds that buy Indian shares. When they sell, they swap rupees for dollars, which weakens the rupee.

viz.l: pulled from Indian stocks in October so far

sources.name: The Hindu
